newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends volatile session mixed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends volatile session mixed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed in choppy dealings on Tuesday, as an afternoon round of fund selling knocked prices off session highs, market sources said.

Most-active May rose to a peak of 174.75 cents before closing at 168.80 cents, up 0.15 cent on the day. May reached a low today of 165.00. July fell 1.35, to 155.60, while the back months closed up 3.85 to down 2.85.

Traders had expected the market to come in between 4.00 and 6.00 cents higher at the opening on the heels of Monday's sharp slid to three-week. But follow through selling by commission houses and a larger-than-expected rise in monthy U.S. consumer coffee stocks weighed on the market from the outset.

GCA data released late Monday showed that supplies of green coffee stowed in U.S. warehouses rose by 204,000 60-kg bags in February to 1,546,000 bags. Most dealers expected the February data to show a rise of up to 100,000 60-kg.
However, commerical interest toward the lows and a last minute run-up in the March contract ahead of today's expiry erased losses and pushed prices into postive territory.
The spot March jumped 11.95 cents, to end at 209.60 cents.
Traders said the market was seen moving sideways in the short term between 160.00 and 190.00 cents per lb basis the May contract in a consolidation phase after recent price volatility.

"Prices will probably consolidate as more coffee comes into the market," said one analyst. He said, however, future prices should continue to be well underpinned by low inventory levels and added that supply concerns were likely to resurface in the coming months.
Technically, May near-term support was seen at 163.00, then 160.00, traders said. Resistance in the May contract was pegged at 175.00-176.00, followed by 190.00.
Turnover was estimated at 15,142 lots, compared with Monday's official tally of 17,862 lots.
